<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via isInput (literal, a string literal in FlowVariableSchema), isOutput (literal, a string literal in FlowVariableSchema))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FlowVariableSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (literal, 41 pages)`, `objectName (literal, 55 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da4f38ae9da1223128edb27c6f21f4bd0a0ac5fc` — the merge of head `62f9f7f6b374705060f4928d1a942eedefa712c7` into base `fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da4f38ae9da1223128edb27c6f21f4bd0a0ac5fc && git checkout da4f38ae9da1223128edb27c6f21f4bd0a0ac5fc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b 62f9f7f6b374705060f4928d1a942eedefa712c7 && git checkout -B drift-repro fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b && git merge --no-ff 62f9f7f6b374705060f4928d1a942eedefa712c7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc55892320869171568f774e0f94a41c28fb8d5b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f06ad2356cf46b1aa061354775084403af371c65`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow.form.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts (the rule `flow-input-unknown-object` and its tests), packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/liveness/flow.json, packages/spec/src/system/flows-translation-face.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.test.ts, .changeset/29442-flow-start-input-record.md, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx and the generated reference rows; read to judge them: packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts and packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (the start doors on main), examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts, packages/spec/liveness/app.json (the planned-row precedent). The rest of the diff (platform-objects bundles and their count pin, validating-metadata.mdx) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Inputs read: card #29442 body and its three comments (triage 6583861409, the Claim 6584041344, the dev report 6585702831), ruling 6580257050 on #29425 in place, PR #29571 body, file list, both comments, and the net diff against `main` at 208d3e2ef; the 68 check-runs on the head, every gate-carrying one `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness), the skips being matrix placeholders and opt-in harnesses.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New optional key `FlowVariableSchema.objectName` — right.** `z.string().regex(/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/).optional()`: the grammar is byte-equal to `ObjectSchema.name` (data/object.zod.ts) and `action.objectName` (ui/action.zod.ts), so the key names an object the way every other authorable object reference does. The published accept set grows by one optional key and nothing an existing flow writes is refused: a widening, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` as declared.
- **Refusal on a non-input — right.** The `.superRefine` refuses `objectName` on a variable whose parsed `isInput !== true` at path `objectName`, code `custom`, with the fix in the message; the test covers the omitted-`isInput` and the `isOutput: true` shapes. `isInput` carries `.default(false)`, and `superRefine` reads the parsed value, so an omitted `isInput` is judged `false` as intended. On zod 4 a refinement is a check on the same object type, so the walkers that need an object shape (`gen:schema`, `gen:docs`, the liveness `childShape`) still descend it — the generated rows in this diff are the evidence.
- **`reference` and `object` as `aliases` — right, and not a conversion.** `strictObject`'s `aliases` are consulted by the unknown-key refusal to name the intended key (`` `reference` → `objectName` ``); the key stays refused, so no ADR-0087 conversion entry is owed. Test pinned.
- **Authorable-surface row `automation/FlowVariable:objectName` — right** (`gen:schema` output; `check:authorable-surface` green).
- **Form repeater column `{ field: 'objectName', label: 'Record Object' }` — right.** The flow form's repeater rows carry names and labels only (the #17508 comment in the file: schema-derived widgets, no `type`), and the label equals the key's `.meta({ title })`, which is what `os i18n extract` keys on; the bundle drift the dev repaired is the mechanical consequence.
- **Lint rule `flow-input-unknown-object` — right as a rule.** It mirrors section 1 of `validateFlowTriggerReadiness` exactly: the same `objectNames` set from `stack.objects`, the same `sys_` exclusion, the same `unknownTriggerObject` verdict (warning with the "another installed package" hedge, `error` with `closureDependencyRemedy` under a stated `packageScope`), under its own id and `where`. It reads the raw `variables` array so the path names the authored entry; the schema owns the input-only shape. Exported from the barrel. The hedged-control test adds the id to the family's severity map.
- **Flows translation-face row `flow.variables[].objectName` → `noReader` — right**: an object name is machine-read, translated under the object's own `objects` entry.
- **Dropped-refinements ledger, one new refinement at 13 sites — right** (judged in ③).
- **Liveness: the `variables` row's note — wrong as the record of a declared-before-enforced key** (judged in ④).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29442-flow-start-input-record.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` on both the PR body and the changeset body, each line-initial. AGENTS.md checklist step 3 and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grade a kind (`added`) at least `minor` on a moved package: spec is moved and `minor`; lint publishes a new rule id and export, `minor` is right for it; platform-objects moves only generated bundle labels, `patch` is right. No `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The level matches what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Spelling `objectName` alone, not `type: 'record'` beside it — the dev's claim verified.** `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts` line 291 declares `{ name: 'completedTask', type: 'record', isInput: false, isOutput: false }`, a variable that holds a WHOLE record written by a `get_record` node's `outputVariable`. `type` is an open string on `FlowVariableSchema` ("Data type (text, number, boolean, object, list)"), so making `'record'` the declaration would give one token two meanings in the shipped corpus (a row on a non-input, an id on an input). Choosing the CRUD nodes' word for the object and leaving `type` as the data type is the right spelling. The maintainer's approval of the new authorable name (triage 6583861409) is a landing condition this record does not grant — escalated, not resolved here.
- **Dropped-refinements row — declaring it dropped is right.** The rule is "`objectName` present ⇒ `isInput === true`", a condition on a VALUE. The closed list in `refinement-projection.ts` has one conditional arm, `dependent-required`, whose docblock states it is presence-only and names exactly this shape (`sslConfig` required when `ssl` is `true`) as not that arm; `isInput` defaults to `false`, so a presence-only projection would accept `{ isInput: false, objectName }` that the runtime refuses, which the list forbids ("an arm that can only approximate its rule does not belong here"). Spelling the rule to project would need a new `if`/`then` arm, a public-contract decision outside this card. The 13 sites are one refinement at the `FlowVariable` root plus `variables.element` under the 12 schemas that embed a flow; the header moves 248/993 → 249/1006 and `build-schemas` (in `TypeScript Type Check`) is green, so the ledger equals the measurement. The alternative, hosting the rule in `FlowSchema`'s existing `superRefine` (zero new sites), would leave the standalone variable parse unenforced; the chosen placement beside the key is the better one. The `ui/ViewFilterOrGroup` block moving below `ui/ViewFilterElement` is the gate's own sort order, no site changed.
- **Open question 1 (approve `objectName`)**: answered as right above; the approval stays the maintainer's.
- **Open question 2 (hold until the server half)**: the dev's own recommendation is B. A hold is a process remedy; the tree is judged in ④ and the defect there is fixable on this branch without a hold.
- **Deviation "`Clause-②` written as `yes (widening)` where the Claim reads bare `yes`"**: the card and the ruling both say `yes (widening)`; measured as one optional key with refusals only on that key — right.
- **Deviation "file surface widened" (platform-objects bundles, validating-metadata.mdx)**: both are consequences of the hits (`check:i18n` drift from the new form row; the closure paragraph naming the new id); in the lane seat's remainder.
- **Deviation "effort at the project default, not xhigh"**: noted; the maintainer sets effort.
- **`Skills-docs:` follow-up owed** (`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` teaches `variables` as `{ name, type, isInput, isOutput }`): correctly left to a Tier H edit; the PR body carries the line.
- **The value is one id, not a list**: the describe says "one record"; a `type: 'list'` input with `objectName` still parses (`type` is open) and the server half will refuse a list value `400` by the describe's own words. Consistent; no flag.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` against ruling A on #29425 and its first consumer.** The key states the rule the ruling binds, word for word: a declared input is loaded from the named object in the caller's own scope at every door that starts the flow by name, `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` unreadable, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` not an id, an undeclared input keeps the visible-read rule. The three doors it names are the three `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts` names on main (the trigger routes, `dispatchFlowAction` over REST and MCP `run_action`, the flow endpoint), and the consumer it points at, `flowDeclaredRecordReads` beside `refuseUnreadableFlowStartRecords`, exists on main and is where the server half plugs `variables[].objectName` in. The TSDoc explains the spelling against the corpus. Read against the lint rule: the schema owns the shape (input-only, an object name), the lint reads only the name against the stack — one judge per fact, no restatement.

**Must-fix — the describe states, as current behaviour, a door rule no door enforces on this head, and the tree marks that nowhere an instrument reads.** The describe is published verbatim into the IDE schema, `/meta/types`, the OpenAPI artifact and `content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx` and `references/api/automation-api.mdx` (both regenerated in this diff), and `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` restates it under "A start input that is a record id" in the present tense. On this head `objectName` is parsed, refused on a non-input and linted, and no door loads it: an author who reads any of those surfaces today will hand a flow an id the caller cannot read and get a run, not a `404`. That is the Prime Directive 10 shape ("declared ≠ enforced ... keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement"), and the repository has a convention for exactly this case: a `planned` liveness row with `authorWarn: true` and an `authorHint`, which `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts` turns into `liveness-planned-property` at `os validate` / `os lint` ("is planned — declared, and a consumer is being built against it (not read YET)"). The precedent is the spec-first contract-split key `app.navigation.dataSource` (#24332, `packages/spec/liveness/app.json`): `status: planned`, `authorWarn: true`, `authorHint: "Keep it, but nothing reads it yet ..."`, flipped to `live` by the commit that lands the reader. This PR instead writes a prose note on the parent `variables` row, which is `live` with the engine as evidence; `check-liveness` grades nothing from a note, and the author-side lint reads only `status` and `authorWarn`, so the note reaches no author and no gate. The route the PR says is closed is open: `flow/variables` sits in `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json`, whose header says a row leaves "by being DRILLED (add `children` with a status + evidence per key)"; `childShape` descends an array's element shape (`flow/nodes` is already drilled one level down), and `getNested` in the author-side lint fans out over arrays, so a drilled `variables.objectName` row warns the author of every flow that writes the key. Remedy on this branch, either arm: (a) drill `flow/variables` — `name`, `type`, `isInput`, `isOutput`, `defaultValue` `live` on the engine evidence the row already cites, `objectName` `planned` with `authorWarn: true`, an `authorHint` naming the server half, and evidence pointing at the refuser (the schema's `superRefine`) the way `api.inputMapping.transform` does — and delete the `flow/variables` baseline row; and qualify the describe and the flows.mdx subsection with the repo's own marker (the `planned` marker regex in `check-liveness.mts` reads `[planned` / `not yet implemented`), so the published text says the doors read the declaration once the server half lands; or (b) land this PR only in the same queue as the server half, with the row `planned` until that PR flips it. Either way the row and the describe stop disagreeing with the tree. A FAIL, as a must-fix is.

**Should-fix — no `os explain` entry for `flow-input-unknown-object`.** Its sibling `flow-trigger-unknown-object` carries `FLOW_TRIGGER_UNKNOWN_OBJECT_EXPLANATION` in `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, and the family's convention (the #22161 comments in section 1) keeps the hint to one remedy line and routes the hedge reasoning — why a name another package declares is not refused, why the closure flips it to `error` — to `os explain`. The new rule has the same hedge and the same closure split and nothing to explain it; the test in `rule-explanations.test.ts` checks only that every entry names an exported id, so no gate catches the omission. Add the entry beside its sibling.

**Should-fix — the `reference` / `object` aliases are right; the `flows.mdx` table row should carry the input-only refusal in its own words.** Minor: the row says "On an input only" and the subsection says it is refused at parse; the generated reference rows say "Only on an input". Consistent enough; no change required if the must-fix edit touches the same paragraph.

**`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.form.ts` against its consumer.** The repeater row follows the file's own #17508 rule (label equal to the schema's `meta.title`, no `type`), the metadata-form bundles carry the four locales, and `check:i18n` is green. Holds. Nothing to fix.

Tried and did not break: `strictObject` + `superRefine` ordering (the unknown-key refusal is terminal and runs first, so the refinement sees only a closed, parsed shape); `lazySchema` over a refined object (the Proxy delegates `_zod`, and `gen:docs` rendered the key); `FlowVariableSchema` consumers needing `.shape` or `.extend` (none outside tests; `flow-variable-scope.ts` reads names only; the console `preview-samples.ts` comment listing four keys is prose); the lint path on a malformed sibling (indexed over the raw array); `sys_` names under a closure (unjudged at both positions, as the trigger's); a `type: 'list'` input with `objectName` (parses; the describe's "one record" is the contract the server half will enforce).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xoyhoi`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbWR3K3h7i1ytwycVg1`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a6ead5ad6aba763274bea9e859097b993b3002c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow.form.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/flow.json (the drilled `variables` rows and their evidence anchors), packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/flow.md, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts and its test (the rule `flow-input-unknown-object`), packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts (its `os explain` entry), packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/flows-translation-face.test.ts, .changeset/29442-flow-start-input-record.md, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx and the two regenerated reference pages; read on `main` at the merge base ce12ad2aa to judge them: packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/FlowRunsPage.tsx, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts and evidence.mts, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts, packages/spec/liveness/app.json (the `navigation.dataSource` precedent), packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts and action-execution.ts (the start doors), packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.test.ts, scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml and lint.yml. The rest of the diff (the four platform-objects metadata-form bundles and their count pin, content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Inputs read: card #29442 body and its four comments (triage 6583861409, the Claim 6584041344, the dev report 6585702831, the claim amendment 6587089741); ruling 6580257050 on #29425 in place; PR #29571 body, its 24-file list, every comment (the docs-drift check, the two contract-review claims, and FAIL record 6587079374 on the older head f06ad2356); the net diff against `main` at the merge base ce12ad2aa; the 65 check-runs on this head: 57 `success`, 8 `skipped`. Every gate-carrying context is `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Check PR Size). `Lint UI` is `skipped` by ci.yml's `filter` job (`needs.filter.outputs.ui != 'false'`): the diff touches no `ui/` path, and the three UI jobs that compile the Console against this spec ran green. The other seven skips are matrix placeholders and opt-in harnesses. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here.

### Resolution of FAIL record 6587079374

- **Must-fix (the describe stated a door rule no door enforces, marked nowhere an instrument reads) — resolved, by arm (a) of that record.** `flow/variables` is drilled: `name`, `isInput`, `defaultValue` cite `dag-traversal.ts#seedDeclaredVariables`, `isOutput` cites `dag-traversal.ts#executeWithoutRetry`, `type` cites `FlowRunsPage.tsx#FlowTestRunner`, each `live`; `objectName` is `planned` with `authorWarn: true`, an `authorHint`, and evidence at `flow.zod.ts#FlowVariableSchema` (the refuser). The `flow/variables` row left `undrilled-containers.baseline.json`; the state-counts shard moves live 36 to 40, planned 2 to 3, classified 38 to 43 (the parent's blanket verdict stops counting, six children count), and `Spec property liveness` is green. The describe opens `[planned]` and says in plain words "No door applies it yet: today the key is parsed and checked, and a start with an id the caller cannot read still runs"; the TSDoc carries a "No door applies it yet" block; flows.mdx carries a `Planned` table row and a warn Callout; the changeset says "The key is **planned**: no door reads it yet". The author-side lint fires: `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` pins `liveness-planned-property` on `variables.objectName` through the shipped ledger and an array of variables, the five live siblings silent.
- **Should-fix (no `os explain` entry) — resolved.** `FLOW_INPUT_UNKNOWN_OBJECT_EXPLANATION` sits beside its sibling in `rule-explanations.ts`, registered under its id, and the rule test's new case checks the hedge and the closure split are explained there while the hint stays one line under 200 characters.

Everything below is re-judged fresh on this head.

### ① Derived judgments
